## TL;DR

The desktop board (720 px and up) now has a search input that writes `q` to the same URL key the phone queue uses. It sits above the existing chip bar, and it reuses the shared predicate and URL helpers in `src/ui-app/src/lib/workQueueFilters.ts` rather than forking them. Most of the work was already committed on this branch by an earlier session. This session confirmed it by reading the code and the tests, and it found that the handoff failure in the queued message was a load-dependent flake in `src/ui-app/tests/agent-review.test.ts`, not a defect on this branch.

## Work and rationale

The branch already held the feature. `src/ui-app/src/components/BoardQueueSearch.vue` is a small controlled input. The URL owns its value, and a local draft keeps typing responsive while the route update commits. A watcher adopts values that arrive from the URL through Back or a shared link, so the draft never lags the route. Clear removes only `q`. `WorkView.vue` renders it only when the effective view is the board, and it writes through `withWorkQueueSearch`, which keeps every other query key, including drawer params and the other quick filters.

I kept the design that the task asked for. The predicate is `matchesWorkQueueFilters`, which the phone queue already uses. The chip bar (`BoardQueueFilters`), Clear filters, and `clearWorkQueueFilterQuery` already read the same keys, so the search input only has to write `q`. When the pipeline view is active, the search box is hidden and the chip bar still says the view does not apply filters.

Tests cover three layers. The desktop-board tests in `work-filter-persistence-qa-browser.test.ts` check that typing writes `q` and keeps the other keys, that a `q` from the URL is reflected and filters the columns, that the clear button removes only `q`, and that the box is absent on the pipeline. The headless WebKit fixtures render the search box at 375, 768 and 1280 px with a long query and assert no horizontal overflow, the input is wider than 120 px, and the clear control is visible. An empty-state case checks that no clear control appears. `work-queue-filters.test.ts` covers the helper additions. `docs/qa/2026-11-filter-persistence-qa.md` was updated: the "no search input at 720 px" gap is replaced by a note that `q` is written from the board and the other quick filters are still set from the phone queue or a link.

## Approaches tried

I considered giving the board its own query parser. I rejected that because the task says to reuse the predicate, and a second parser would drift from the phone queue. I also considered writing `q` on every keystroke versus debouncing. I kept one route update per input event, because `router.replace` is cheap here and a debounce would make the URL lag behind what the user sees, which breaks reload behaviour.

I did not change the search-box layout beyond what the existing styles needed. The fixtures show the box fits at all three widths.

## Challenges and blockers

The queued message reported a failure in `src/ui-app/tests/agent-review.test.ts`, "routes reviewer chat to its own session and serves the conversation". That test is about the reviewer chat, not the work board, and it is not touched by this branch. I ran it alone and the whole file. Both runs passed all 17 tests, so I did not change it. The likely cause is timing under load, since the test waits on a log-file count written by a fake reviewer process. I did not widen timeouts or edit the test without reproducing the failure. If the gate fails again on the same test, that is a real timing problem to look at separately.

## Key learnings

The task description was partly out of date. The feature had already been built in earlier commits, so the useful work this session was verifying it against the acceptance criteria and checking the gate. A test that fails once in a gate but passes alone and as a file is a flake until it reproduces on an idle machine. Running the test file in isolation was the cheap way to tell.
